files.label: WordPress user list (usernames for login attacks)

findings.title: FTP (file transfer) reachable from the internet (port 21)
findings.impact: An extra door into your infrastructure that attackers will try to open.
findings.fix: Close the port in your firewall or restrict it to a VPN / allow-list.

findings.title: DMARC is in monitor-only mode (p=none)
findings.impact: You can see spoofing but nothing is stopped.

findings.title: SSH (remote admin) reachable from the internet (port 22)
findings.impact: An extra door into your infrastructure that attackers will try to open.
findings.fix: Close the port in your firewall or restrict it to a VPN / allow-list.

findings.title: Publicly downloadable: WordPress user list (usernames for login attacks)
findings.impact: Gives attackers a map of your system.
findings.fix: Block access to this path on your web server.

findings.title: CMS version published: WordPress 7.1.4
findings.impact: Bots scan the internet for exactly this string the day a new exploit drops.
findings.fix: Remove the generator meta tag and keep the CMS updated.

findings.title: DNSSEC not enabled
findings.impact: DNS answers for your domain can be forged to redirect visitors.
findings.fix: Enable DNSSEC at your registrar/DNS provider.

findings.title: Publicly downloadable: WordPress XML-RPC (password brute-force amplifier)
findings.impact: Gives attackers a map of your system.
findings.fix: Block access to this path on your web server.

findings.title: No CAA record
findings.impact: Any certificate authority may issue certificates for your domain.
findings.fix: Add a CAA record naming your certificate provider.

findings.title: No security.txt contact
findings.impact: Researchers who find a hole in your site have no way to tell you before criminals find it.

findings.title: Valid HTTPS certificate
findings.impact: Traffic between customers and your site is encrypted.

findings.title: All key security headers present
findings.impact: Browsers are told to enforce strong protections on your site.

findings.title: Clean on 4 threat-intelligence blocklists
findings.impact: Your domain is not currently flagged for malware or phishing.
findings.detail: Cloudflare Malware Shield, Quad9 Threat Blocking, CleanBrowsing Security, AdGuard DNS

ai.headline: Our website has several open doors that hackers could exploit.
ai.summary: Attackers could use open admin ports and leaked usernames to hijack our site or steal data. This risks significant reputational damage and potential financial loss from a service outage. These gaps are common and can be closed quickly with standard security updates.
actions: Close open FTP and SSH admin ports immediately
Hide WordPress usernames and disable XML-RPC
Update email security settings to block spoofing
ai.boardLine: We have identified a few security gaps and are implementing fixes to harden our digital perimeter.
